summary: Database connectivity failure on api-gateway causing cascading service degradation. postgres-primary experienced connection timeouts leading to pool exhaustion and circuit breaker activation. Service partially recovered using Redis cache fallback.
root_cause: PostgreSQL primary database (postgres-primary:5432) became unresponsive, causing connection timeouts (30s) and exhausting the connection pool (0/20 available). This triggered circuit breaker activation and 503 errors on user-facing endpoints.
evidence: 4 ERROR-level events in 10 seconds indicating rapid failure cascade
Connection timeout to postgres-primary:5432 repeated twice within 4 seconds
Connection pool fully exhausted: 0/20 connections available
HTTP 503 errors returned to clients on /api/v1/users
Circuit breaker transitioned to OPEN state for postgres-primary
Recovery observed at 14:31:00 — connection restored after ~60 seconds
recommendations: Investigate PostgreSQL primary for resource exhaustion, lock contention, or network issues
Increase connection pool size from 20 to 50 with proper timeout configuration
Implement connection pool warm-up and health-check queries
Add read replica for read-heavy endpoints to reduce primary load
Configure PgBouncer as a connection pooler in front of PostgreSQL
Set up proactive alerting on connection pool utilization > 80%
anomalies_detected: Complete connection pool exhaustion (0/20) — indicates no connection recycling
30-second timeout suggests TCP-level connectivity issue, not query slowness
Recovery after 60 seconds without intervention — possibly transient network issue
